marc:datafield.marc:subfield: Elimination of TRIMs : the experience of selected developing countries
UNCTAD current studies on FDI and development, no. 5

The World Trade Organization Agreement on Trade-Related Investment Measures (TRIMs) came into force in 1995, as part of the Uruguay Round negotiations. This study considers the experience of four countries that notified TRIMs in 1995: Argentina, Mexico, Pakistan and the Philippines. It also includes two countries that, when the project was started, were seeking to accede to WTO: Ethiopia adn Viet Nam. The idea of including these two countries was to examine the likely impact of WTO accession on their use of selected TRIMs. The study suggests that the extent to which TRIMs have helped advance economic development has varied considerably, reflecting the specific economic conditions and policy environment of the country using them. The effectiveness of various TRIMs has been influenced by a range of factors, including government capabilities, local absorptive capacity of the workforce and domestic enterprises, and the extent to which measures used have been comparible with other industrial and trade policies
